thread:
alex: Thinking out loud — proposal to reduce paging noise by combining per-cardinality coalescing with a region-fallback path. idea: if an alert fires with >N unique hosts, create a ticket; if it's low-cardinality but recurring across many regions within a short window, page.
morgan: Nice. So basically invert the usual rule: page only when cardinality low (high-impact single node) OR cross-region correlated spikes, otherwise ticket. want to see thresholds.
jamie: Agree. We should also add a per-alert cooldown that scales with cardinality. e.g. cooldown = min(30m, 5m * cardinality). prevents 100 tiny pages.
tay: Can we codify into a Prometheus suppression rule? something like:
```
alert: GPU_P95_Spike
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance, region)) > 1.2
labels:
  severity: ticket
annotations:
  summary: "p95 gpu latency spike"
  description: "{{ $labels.instance }}"
```
and then a webhook that inspects `count by (instance)` and escalates to `pager` if count==1 or count>3 across regions.
jamie: I'd rather keep logic in Alertmanager routing than a webhook if possible. you can use grouping_key and a custom continue: true route that matches on `instance` cardinality via `group_wait` changes.
alex: True, but Alertmanager can't natively count unique label values. webhook + small lambda could do uniqueness scoring fast. pros: flexible; cons: more moving parts.
devon: What about using Prometheus recording rules to maintain a rolling unique count per alert name? we can approximate with `count_values` or `count by (instance)` over vector, then check threshold in rule itself.
morgan: For region-fallback, we should have a short window (5m) to consider cross-region correlation. if same alert hits us-east & eu-west within 5m, escalate regardless of cardinality.
sre-bot: [automated] in last 24h: 42 GPU_P95_Spike alerts, 31 tickets, 11 pages. median cardinality=4. avg time-to-ack for pages=3m.
alex: Good data. I want a conservative rollout: implement scoring webhook behind feature flag for 72h against staging and one small prod cluster, then flip on for all non-prod.
jamie: Runbook changes: add a decision matrix — when webhook returns `severity=pager` it should include `reason=single-instance|cross-region|hotshard` and link to the appropriate playbook. Also include an automatic re-route to ticket if no ack in 10m.
tay: For `hotshard` detection, add a check: if top-1 instance contributes >70% of error rate in last 2m, treat as single-node page.
devon: Cost angle: fewer pages -> fewer wakeups -> lower ops cost, but we must ensure SLOs for customer-facing prod routes aren't diluted. we'll run a short SLO regression: simulate pages suppressed and check 99th percentile user latency delta.
morgan: Experiment plan:
  - phase 1: webhook + feature flag (staging + canary prod) 72h
  - phase 2: enable for non-critical clusters 1w
  - phase 3: full enable with monitoring + rollback metric (increase in user p99 > 0.5%)
alex: Who owns the webhook and alert-rule edits? jamie for Alertmanager changes, devon for recording rules and histograms, tay for runbook edits. i'll own rollout and metrics.
jamie: I'll push a draft prometheus rule for the unique-count approach tonight and drop link. will also add `group_interval` experiments.
alex: :thumbsup: Let's aim to ship the draft and schedule a 30-min dry-run sync tomorrow at 11am.
morgan: noted. i'll prepare the SLO regression harness.
sre-bot: [automated] meeting created: "Alert coalescing dry-run" 11:00 tomorrow (30m). attendees: alex, jamie, devon, tay, morgan.
